chapters: In the beginning was the Word

events.text: Black. Silence. A single drop of water falls into still black water: one ripple, and at its centre one tiny point of light.
The drop. Silence.

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: Let there be light,
The point of light bursts outward: pure white-gold light floods out in every direction, filling everything. Light only, no stars, no galaxies (the stars come on Day Four).
The burst: one frame of silence, then a deep boom and the score's first great swell.

Montage in Genesis order, about one second a shot, the score driving: the deep, the sky, land rising, forests, sea creatures, herds, the man and the woman far off in a garden, the flood, Abraham under the stars, the brick pits of Egypt, the tabernacle in the wilderness, Jerusalem at dawn, the garden tomb with its stone rolled away (no figures), the long road of the centuries, a city of today at night seen from far above.
Through all of history to today.
Everything rushes backward, faster and faster, and collapses into a single point of light. Silence. The point drifts and becomes a spark rising from a kiln fire in Egypt at night (match cut).
Rewind into a single point; silence; the spark.
Egypt at night: brick pits by firelight, mud moulds slapped full, the brick-maker's mud-caked hands. He straightens and lifts his eyes to the sky.
Wet clay, fire, distant work drums.

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: Let Us make man in Our image,
Hold on the brick-maker, chest up, firelight on his face; then black.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Every nation told a story of how the world began. In Babylon's, people were made to carry the labour of the gods. Then a nation of slaves heard this one.
THE SEVEN DAYS / Genesis 1:1 to 2:3
Title over dark water. Low hit, one swell, then quiet.

The Nile at blazing dawn; kilns and stacked mud bricks; a clay tablet pressed with wedge script; a storm over a dark sea. Objects and landscapes only. The brick-maker once more, at work under the sun.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Israel first heard these words as the opening of the Torah, given through Moses to a people who had spent generations in Egypt.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: In Babylon, the god Marduk defeats the sea goddess Tiamat and splits her body to form sky and earth. Human beings are made to carry the labour of the gods, so that the gods may rest.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: In Egypt, the sun was worshipped as a god, and Pharaoh was presented as a son of the sun.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Moses wanted Israel to know who their God was before they learned anything else about Him. Not one god among many, but the Maker of the sun that Egypt worshipped, the sea that the nations feared, and the land they were about to enter.
Hard cut to black and silence.
Black water under no light; a slow push across the surface of the deep.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Now the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.
Wind moving across the water, spray lifting: the Spirit by effect only, never a figure or a bird.
Wind passes across the water. Hold.

Stillness; a single drop falls into the black water (the sound of the opening); then the horizon ignites and light floods across the water, black turning to gold; two and three second cuts, then one long wide. Day beside night; evening, then morning.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let there be light,”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: and there was light.
Set piece: the light breaks. The score crests above where the voice sat.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.” And there was evening, and there was morning, the first day.
The frame builds from the film's own shots: three realms on the left, their three fillings on the right, the seventh day above. Cards slide in with soft hits.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Verse two names the problem. The earth was formless and void. In Hebrew, tohu wabohu.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Days one to three give shape to the formless: light from darkness, the waters above from the waters below, the sea from the dry land.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Days four to six fill the void: lights for the light, birds and fish for the sky and sea, animals and people for the land.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And the seventh day stands apart, as the goal.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Over the deep, the Spirit of God is hovering, the same word used of an eagle over its young. Attentively near, poised to bring life.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Light on the first day, before the sun on the fourth. The point is theological before it is astronomical: light comes from God.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: So first, God gives the world its shape.
Waters rise and part; an expanse opens between the waters above and below, light like beaten gold. No sun, moon or stars.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let there be an expanse between the waters, to separate the waters from the waters.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: So God made the expanse and separated the waters beneath it from the waters above. And it was so.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God called the expanse “sky.” And there was evening, and there was morning, the second day.
Seas draw back and dry land rises streaming; grass, seed plants and fruit trees race across the hills in two second time-lapse cuts with whooshes.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let the waters under the sky be gathered into one place, so that the dry land may appear.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And it was so.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God called the dry land “earth,” and the gathering of waters He called “seas.” And God saw that it was good.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let the earth bring forth vegetation: seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each bearing fruit with seed according to its kind.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And it was so.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The earth produced vegetation: seed-bearing plants according to their kinds and trees bearing fruit with seed according to their kinds. And God saw that it was good.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And there was evening, and there was morning, the third day.
Montage at full drive, then the music stops on a wide, green, empty world.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Now the three realms stand ready: the light, the sky and the sea, and the dry land. The formless has been given shape.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: But it is still empty.
Silence.
Black sky over the new land; the first sunrise lifts over the sea in one long take.
The score rises with the light.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let there be lights in the expanse of the sky to distinguish between the day and the night, and let them be signs to mark the seasons and days and years.

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: And let them serve as lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And it was so.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night. And He made the stars as well.
Moon and stars over the land at night.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God set these lights in the expanse of the sky to shine upon the earth,

events.speaker: READER
events.text: to preside over the day and the night, and to separate the light from the darkness. And God saw that it was good.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And there was evening, and there was morning, the fourth day.
Cut to Egypt's sun blazing over the brick pits; the brick-maker shades his eyes.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Notice what is not said. The sun and moon are not even named. To Egypt the sun was a god. Here they are the greater light and the lesser light, lamps hung in the sky with a job to do, and the stars are mentioned almost in passing.
A lamp's flame in darkness, then the sun again.
Shoals turning in the light; a whale rising from the deep and breaching in slow motion; flocks lifting off the water into the sky. Two to four second cuts.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let the waters teem with living creatures, and let birds fly above the earth in the open expanse of the sky.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: So God created the great sea creatures and every living thing that moves, with which the waters teemed according to their kinds, and every winged bird after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then God blessed them and said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And there was evening, and there was morning, the fifth day.
The breach: impact, spray, wingbeats.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The great sea creatures, a word that elsewhere names the monsters of the sea, are simply creatures God made and blessed.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And for the first time, God blesses. The whole account moves from emptiness to fullness, because God gives.
Herds across the plains: aurochs, gazelle, ibex, dust and running. The most driving pulse in the film.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let the earth bring forth living creatures according to their kinds: livestock, land crawlers, and beasts of the earth according to their kinds.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And it was so.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God made the beasts of the earth according to their kinds, the livestock according to their kinds, and everything that crawls upon the earth according to its kind. And God saw that it was good.
The herds slow; the plain empties to first light. The music cuts to nothing.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Then the pattern breaks. God does not simply say, let there be. He deliberates.
Black, then dawn coming up very slowly.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself, and every creature that crawls upon it.”
The man and the woman in the new world at first light (The Garden's cast, photoreal rules).

events.speaker: READER
events.text: So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them.
Set piece: the image of God. The second peak, warm and immense, no narration.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Three lines of poetry, and the word created sounds three times.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Image, tselem, is the word used for a carved image, the kind Israel was told to destroy in Canaan. In a world full of idols, God places His own living image on the earth.
The brick-maker's face, chest up, in firelight.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Remember who first heard this. Slaves who had been treated as tools in Pharaoh's building projects are told that every human being, male and female, is made in the image of God and blessed with a royal calling.
Fields of grain and fruit trees, the man and the woman far off among them.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: God blessed them and said to them,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it; rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth.”

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Humanity is not made to feed the gods. God feeds humanity.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then God said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “Behold, I have given you every seed-bearing plant on the face of all the earth, and every tree whose fruit contains seed. They will be yours for food.

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: And to every beast of the earth and every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth, everything that has the breath of life in it, I have given every green plant for food.”

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And it was so.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the sixth day.
The whole world in golden light, wide.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Seven times God looks and calls it good. The last time, very good. The goodness of the world is not a human judgment, but His.
The finished world in long golden light; nothing moves but light and breath.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Then the pattern breaks altogether.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were completed in all their vast array.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And by the seventh day God had finished the work He had been doing; so on that day He rested from all His work.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it, because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.
Silence but for the room tone of a finished world.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: There is no speech. No it was good. No evening and morning. And the Hebrew names the seventh day three times in two verses.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: God does not rest because He is tired. He rests because the work is finished, and good.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Then He blesses a day and sanctifies it, the first thing in the Bible to be made holy. Time itself belongs to Him.
Evening in the wilderness: the brick-maker's family resting together.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Israel's own week was patterned on this one.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: But the passage itself presses a different question. Not how long God took, but who He is, and whose the world is.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.text: A single point of light in total darkness.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The New Testament does not treat Christ as a latecomer to this story. It places Him at its beginning.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: READER
events.text: In the beginning was the Word,

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: READER
events.text: Through Him all things were made, and without Him nothing was made that has been made,

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.text: The point widens into dawn.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Genesis shows God creating by speaking. John tells us that the Speech itself is a person, and that He became flesh.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: READER
events.text: The Light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.text: A garden at first light; the stone rolled back from an empty tomb, no figures.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The first creation climbed toward a seventh day. Jesus lies in the tomb through the Sabbath, and rises on the first day of the week. The new creation begins on the first day of a new week.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.text: Set piece: the empty tomb at dawn. The third peak, no narration.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.text: Light on the path out of the tomb.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Humanity was made to be God's image. Christ is the image of the invisible God, the true Man in whom the human calling is finally carried out.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And the rest of the seventh day, He offers in person.

events.chapter: In the beginning was the Word
events.speaker: READER
events.text: Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest,
The deep returning over the land, creation undone; then a radiant new world with no sun in the sky and no sea.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: This page sets the standard for everything after it. Chapter three is a tragedy because chapter one was very good. Death, violence and exile are wrong because they were not part of the world God made.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And the last pages of the Bible deliberately echo the first. A new heaven and a new earth. A city that has no need of sun or moon, for the glory of God is its light. The sea is no more.

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: Behold, I make all things new.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The story that began with, In the beginning God, ends with God dwelling among His people in a world made new.
The new creation: radiant swell.
The dark deep with light breaking across it, as at the start.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: On the first day God said, let there be light, before the sun existed, because light comes from Him.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Where do you need to ask God to speak light into a dark place?
Hold on the light.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Genesis one is the wide shot. In chapter two, the camera comes down to the ground, to the dust, and to a garden.
A frame of The Garden; then the end card with the study link and a WATCH NEXT space.

End card.
